#2046. Arsenal Women held by London City Lionesses despite Frida Maanum goal

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal Women missed the chance to end their frustrating run of draws at home as London City Lionesses came from behind to earn a 1-1 draw at the Emirates Stadium.

Frida Maanum gave the Gunners the lead in an exciting start to the game. But Isobel Goodwin equalised almost straight away. Despite creating plenty of chances, Renée Slegers’ side failed to find a second goal.

Arsenal have now lost their last five WSL games at the Emirates. The results were yet another frustrating afternoon for the defending champions, who put in a strong display against Barcelona in Europe earlier in the week.

Arsenal started on a high note, creating some dangerous chances with their quick play. Emily Fox and Lisa Baum worked really well together down the right, and Ona Batlle had a great chance from the edge of the box.

As the pressure mounted, Fox surged forward and played a perfectly weighted through ball to Alessia Russo. The striker turned and played the ball back to Maanum, who rounded off her impressive comeback from injury by finishing.

Arsenal had little time to rejoice. London City equalised just a minute later as Goodwin found herself in space to fire past Misa Rodríguez.

The visitors looked more confident after equalising, but Mary Earps was proving a tough ask for Arsenal to score past. The ex-Manchester United shot-stopper kept out Baum and made some key stops from Arsenal’s efforts.

Rodriguez also had to make a key stop before half-time as she got a hand to Daniela Arques Lazaro’s powerful strike to keep the scores level.

The Gunners continued their attacking play but were made to work hard by a high pressing side from London City.

But Arsenal still managed to create some chances. Caitlin Foord put Earps under pressure and Maanum and Baum combined before the latter saw her curl just wide.

London City posed a threat too. With Kadidiatou Diani and Grace Geyoro causing defensive problems for Arsenal, Geyoro fired into the side netting.

Delphine Cascarino had the game’s defining moment of the second half, hitting the crossbar from outside the box. However, Arsenal were lucky to escape and Maanum came close to winning the game, hitting the woodwork from a dangerous counter.

Slegers brought on Kyra Cooney-Cross and Olivia Smith in the 72nd minute to provide some new energy. Smith looked lively upon entering the game, but Earps denied her efforts and Batlle’s cross.

Emily Fox had to be substituted due to injury in the final moments of the game, but Slegers later indicated that she would be okay.

The Gunners were unable to find a winning goal and will now turn their attention to their Champions League clash on Thursday with Lyon. They will then face West Ham at home in the WSL.

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Declan Rice’s new contract shows how much of an asset he is to Mikel Arteta. His recent performances show why.

The England international has reportedly signed a new five-year deal which will keep him at the Emirates Stadium until 2031. The contract is a reward for the midfielder who has been instrumental in Arsenal’s success since he moved to the club in 2023 from West Ham.

Rice has not just provided the presence and protection that Arsenal were hoping for with their £105 million signing. He has continued to develop his game, especially after returning to his deeper midfield role this season.

Rice came in as a defensive midfielder, but Arteta quickly saw how much he could offer higher up the park.

His physicality, ability to run into the box and set piece threat made him a useful left-sided number eight. Rice had a huge impact in midfield for Arsenal, bringing goals and a new attacking threat.

But Rice has played in a more advanced position on the right-hand side of the midfield duo this season, and this has not limited his impact but instead highlighted another key part of his game.

Rice has made the most line-breaking passes in the Premier League this season, with Opta stats reported by Sky Sports showing he is second only to Premier League players.

This is of particular interest, as he has often come under criticism for his distribution. But he is averaging nearly double the amount of line-breaking passes he did last season.

While his running ability is still an asset, he is also becoming much better at penetrating through the defensive lines to find his teammates, giving Arsenal another option to move the ball forward with.

The development of Rice is key in securing a new contract at Arsenal.

The 27-year-old has already proven to be one of the most reliable members of Arteta’s squad and has shown great longevity by only missing five games out of his 119 Premier League outings in his first spell at the club.

Former West Ham teammate Jack Wilshere has also praised Rice’s strong work ethic, ability to adapt and natural leadership qualities.

The reported 5-year deal will keep Rice at Arsenal until 2031, into his early 30s. While the terms of the deal have yet to be signed, it is a huge statement from the club.

They are not only rewarding Rice for what he has done but also investing in what he can do.

With Arteta finding new ways to utilise Rice’s qualities in midfield, Rice could still have some of his best years ahead of him.

Martin Zubimendi has raised questions among Arsenal fans over his future. This follows comments from the midfielder that he is keen to succeed in north London despite struggling for game time this season.

The Spain international has been linked with a move to Chelsea, Atletico Madrid and Real Madrid ahead of the January transfer window. Reports from Spain have said that Zubimendi’s situation at the club is becoming more complex, with the player possibly being available.

Zubimendi has also spoken about the speculation. In his interview during the international break with Marca, he said he did not feel like he was near to a move to Atletico, and he is still delighted to be in London.

He added the 27-year-old has had no contact with any other clubs. His priority is to get into Arteta’s squad.

This is an interesting response to the transfer speculation that has been building. Arsenal may well attract interest for one of their midfielders. However, there does not appear to be any evidence that Zubimendi is actively looking to leave.

In his first season, he played 38 times in the Premier League and became an important member of Arteta’s midfield. However, he has not started a league game this season.

Opta Analyst shows that he has only played 100 minutes in the Premier League in seven games. He has also faced increased competition for a spot in the team with the arrival of Bruno Guimarães.

Myles Lewis-Skelly is also an option in the middle of the park. Zubimendi will have to fight for his place back.

It is understood Arteta had a chat with Zubimendi ahead of the campaign and made it clear he would face more competition from the new signings and would have to earn his place.

Zubimendi has accepted the challenge and has said he could see it as a chance to learn and improve due to his reduced workload.

The interest from Spain and Chelsea will make it a tough choice if the right offers come in. However, losing Zubimendi will mean Arteta won’t have as many options to call upon in the busy second half of the season.

But he proved his worth in the game against Slavia Prague earlier this month. He started the Champions League match and played the full 90 minutes.

This shows that his contribution shouldn’t be judged purely on how much he plays in the Premier League. Arsenal will have a busy schedule in Europe and domestically, and he may provide some much-needed quality in the midfield.

With Zubimendi contracted until 2030, there is no immediate reason for Arsenal to look to sell him. He will have time to fight for his spot in the starting XI.

Despite not making a commitment to remain at the club beyond January, his remarks indicate that he is not on the lookout for alternatives.

The priority for Arsenal will be trying to find a way to get the best out of Zubimendi. He was a regular last season and seems happy to wait for his chance.

Viktor Gyökeres is reminding Arsenal of his prolific goal scoring capabilities.

The striker found the back of the net twice in Sweden’s 3-2 Nations League win against Bosnia and Herzegovina on November 14, both times from the spot to take his total to four in the Nations League this season.

The win also means they have booked their place in League A with one match left to play in the group, and Gyökeres has certainly played his part in this excellent run.

However, the performance will raise questions about his future at the club. The idea that he may be leaving in January is a possibility that needs to be looked at.

However, he has had more opportunities to play in European competition. Gyökeres has started three of Arsenal’s four matches in the Champions League, scoring one goal and providing two assists.

Gyökeres is not totally out of Arteta’s plans, but he will not play much domestically.

He has been in fine form internationally recently. Sweden are building their attack around his movement and penalty area presence, meaning he will have chances to regularly perform.

There have been suggestions surrounding Gyökeres’ future, with reports that Arsenal may look to add more attacking flair to their squad.

For now, though, there is little evidence that Gyökeres is trying to leave the club.

Beppe Marotta featured in the first episode of ‘L’impresa sportiva’, a segment on Il Sole 24 ORE’s TV program dedicated to the world of sport. He spoke about foreign ownership in Italy and the new stadium project, with his words via MilanPress.

“Football is a powerfully unifying phenomenon. After religion, I believe only sport can unite people by breaking down barriers. However, it’s also become a business. There are 12 foreign owners out of 20 in Serie A,” he began.

“On the one hand, there’s a decline, on the other, we have to ask ourselves what would have happened to football in Italy without these foreign owners. It’s no coincidence that the future stadium is a joint venture between the two Milan clubs, both of which have American owners with, frankly, very farsighted vision.

#2039. Gary Neville launches surprise defence of Diogo Dalot and names the THREE defenders Mauricio Pochettino should sell before Man United boo boy

Published: 10:42 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 12:38 EST, 17 November 2026

Gary Neville has stood up for under-fire Manchester United man Diogo Dalot – and named three of his defensive team-mates he would rather see leave the club before him.

The Portugal international's limp performances have come under heavy scrutiny this season with the decline of Michael Carrick's side as autumn has worn on.

But as Mauricio Pochettino prepares to take over at Old Trafford, Neville urged the new manager not to immediately expel the defender, despite his drop-off in form.

'I think if he was in a decent back four he'd be alright,' Neville told Stick to United co-host Mark Goldbridge on Tuesday. 'But he's got a shocking back four alongside him.

'Positionally he's not great. He could be better on the ball. He could be better at everything he does. Of course he could. I just think he's such an easy target, Dalot. I honestly do.'

Neville admitted that sometimes he listens to his fellow Man United-supporting friends deriding Dalot and wonders 'are they watching something that I don't see?'

Gary Neville has defended Man United star Diogo Dalot - arguing that he has team-mates who are far weaker

The Portugal international has come in for heavy criticism from supporters this season

But in his opinion, there are three defenders that he would let go in the 'first wave' of changes in Manchester.

'I'd be getting (Noussair) Mazraoui well gone before him,' he continued. 'I'd be getting (Lisandro) Martinez gone well before him. I'll be getting (Matthijs) De Ligt gone well before him.

'(De Ligt has) got one big problem. He doesn’t play football. If a player is injury prone and doesn't play football, just because he hasn't played doesn't mean to say that he should go above a player who's played every single week and he's throwing his hand up. You want someone who's actually reliable and play. De Ligt has to go. De Ligt, Martinez, Mazraoui.'

Another stalwart in the team that Neville was keen to have a second chance under Pochettino was Luke Shaw.

'He will keep Shaw because he knows him and he'll probably get the best out of him. The problem with Luke is injuries,' he added. 'So he'll have to manage him. So he'll have to bring a left back in. But let's just say who he'll keep.

'He'll keep Shaw. He'll keep (Harry) Maguire because he'll trust him and he'll think that he's basically a soldier and someone who can do a job for him.

'He'll keep (Leny) Yoro because I think he'll think "I've got something there that I can work with". (But) I think he's a little bit gangly, all over the place right now. And he looks like he's going to slip every time. He's got that sort of Bambi-on-ice (look).

'Physically what will happen is with Yoro, he'll go one way or the other. I like the fact he's been brought into the French team. It tells me sometimes you just have got to connect the dots and think, "okay, well, if they think he's good, then we must be missing something here because we're not seeing it yet, are we?".'

Neville went on to suggest that Yoro was lacking the connection within his body that Premier League rivals such as Jeremy Jacquet are already able to harness – something Sir Alex Ferguson had identified in Rio Ferdinand when he was at West Ham.

Like Ferdinand, Neville backed Yoro to flourish as he taps into that connection and improves his strength and stability.

'So Yoro he will keep: Yoro, Maguire and Shaw I think he'll keep and I think he'll keep Dalot. To start with,' Neville said. 'He'll have to bring in three defenders to go above them. Let's be clear. He'll have to bring in three defenders.

'Mazraoui I would lose, De Ligt I would lose because he's injury prone. Martinez 100 per cent. 100 per cent. 100 per cent.'

As well as struggling for form this season, Martinez has been a challenging presence in the Man United squad this term, boldly calling out the Man United hierarchy during a firebrand interview last month.

Neville was more interested in new head coach Mauricio Pochettino despatching Noussair Mazraoui and Matthijs de Ligt

Lisandro Martinez has been an unsettled presence in the side this season and hit out at the club's recruiting last month

The Argentina star implied that he was disappointed with the club's recruitment strategy over the summer, and was forced to hold clear-the-air talks to smooth his return to the side.

Neville added that he would send Ayden Heaven on loan to get experience in the lower divisions to 'build' his ability up, as it was borderline 'unfair' to be 'putting him in' the side at present.

But not all of the changes can come quickly for Pochettino, who has little time before taking charge of Man United against Liverpool at Anfield this weekend.

'First wave, end of the season,' Neville clarified of what he believes Pochettino's plan for change will be. 'No, he can't get rid of (them all) in January.

'He has to bring one or two defenders in January if he can. But he can't get rid of all those in his first wave. He's only got one month till January.'

The drawn-out process of sacking Carrick began last week when Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada flew to Monaco for talks with co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer ownership group.

While his future was on the chopping block, Carrick held training sessions at Carrington before the axe finally swung last Thursday.

Pochettino was appointed days later and gave a tearful farewell press conference ahead of his penultimate game with the United States national team on Saturday.

‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he told the press. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay. I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'

#2038. Arsenal mourns Peter Storey: 1971 Double-winning hero dies aged 81

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal have expressed their condolences in the passing of former player Peter Storey.

Storey was an influential member of one of the most successful sides in the club’s history. The midfielder appeared in 501 games for the Gunners between 1965 and 1977, winning the First Division and FA Cup during the 1970/71 season.

Storey was a key figure in the famous run as he helped keep the FA Cup hopes alive with a display against Stoke City.

A statement from the club confirmed his death on Tuesday (17th November). The club will pay tribute to Storey in their Champions League tie against Borussia Dortmund on 24th November.

Storey signed as an apprentice with Arsenal in 1961, and made his first-team debut in October 1965 in a game against Leicester City.

He was later converted to a central midfielder by manager Bertie Mee and coach Don Howe. Storey became an invaluable member of the squad due to his aggressive play, work-rate and versatility.

In 1970 Storey was part of the side that won the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, and the following year Arsenal won the league and FA Cup double.

Storey played a key role in an amazing FA Cup semi-final in April 1971. After Arsenal had looked like they were losing, Storey scored a last-minute penalty to make it 2-2.

Arsenal won the replay to get to the final, beating Liverpool to win their first-ever double.

Storey scored 17 goals in 501 games for Arsenal. This puts him in joint 8th place in the most appearances for the club.

Storey enjoyed success at club level and earned his first cap for England in 1971. He earned a total of 19 caps for England.

He played for England until 1973. In 1977, Storey left Arsenal to join Fulham, meaning he had a 12-year stint at the north London club.

He played 19 games for Fulham before retiring from professional football in 1978.

Following his football career, Storey had a difficult time. He was imprisoned for a number of crimes. In 2010, he wrote an autobiography, True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man, detailing these events in his life.

He will be remembered in Arsenal history for his impressive contribution to the club. Having made 501 appearances for the club, he was a key member of the squad that won the Double in 1971.

Playing against Borussia Dortmund will be a great way for fans to pay tribute to one of the key players in a special time in the history of the club.

#2036. GdS: Why Cardinale’s ‘those two million’ comment signifies Milan’s change in tact

Gerry Cardinale declared that AC Milan will alter the way they plan for preseason, but what exactly could that mean?

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, the pile of rubble created six months ago by Milan’s defeat to Cagliari brought about a managerial and sporting revolution, and it is still going on. Cardinale continues to alter the way the club do things, hoping to evolve into an efficient and successful organisation.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In his interview with the newspaper a few days ago, the owner extended the discussion even to the scheduling of preseason tours, stating: “Those two million for a friendly match overseas will no longer be our objective, as they were in the past.”

Beyond the actual practical implications, these words reveal a new stance: from now on, throughout the summer, sporting priorities will take precedence over financial ones. In other words, if the opportunity arises to play a friendly match outside of Europe, Amorim will be consulted.

The Rossoneri also intend to become an active participant in organising their own summer commitments. They will no longer simply put forward their availability in exchange for an offer from some tournament, but rather being the architects of their own program.

These details clearly illustrate the ownership’s shift, but in recent days there is talk of a €70m bid for Endrick, the €60m pursuit of Nicolo Tresoldi and the potential €40m acquisition of Goncalo Inacio, the money has to keep coming in.

Cardinale injected €50m in equity into the club’s coffers, earmarked for sports needs. This injection was made to make up for the loss of Champions League revenue. It’s the first time RedBird has injected cash for this purpose, with the other being €55m to buy land in San Donato.

That’s why, in this context, it’s no longer surprising when Cardinale says that ‘those €2m paid for a friendly match overseas will no longer be our goal’. The bar has been raised, with the aim of trophies being raised down the line.

#2031. Newcastle vs Arsenal: Team news, predicted line-ups and match preview

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal will have a tough task on hand as they visit St James’ Park.

Mikel Arteta’s side are five points clear at the top of the Premier League after their 1-0 victory over Hull City ahead of the international break. The Gunners have now gone nine games unbeaten in all competitions.

Despite only one win in their last six games, Newcastle will be a dangerous side at home.

Although Arsenal have won the last three encounters with Newcastle, recent games at Tyneside have not gone entirely smoothly for Mikel Arteta. He will also have to make a few key decisions in the squad with players injured and a busy run of fixtures.

Bruno Guimaraes will certainly be a topic of discussion for this game. The midfielder joined Newcastle four-and-a-half years ago, playing an important role in the development of the side, before moving to Arsenal on a reported 75 million pound move in the summer.

Whilst he has struggled to make himself an automatic starter in Arteta’s side, he could have a bigger impact with the absence of Martin Zubimendi.

Zubimendi is likely to be out for several weeks. Declan Rice should start, and Guimaraes is also likely to be involved, to form a double pivot.

Newcastle will try to play a gritty game to unsettle Arsenal. Despite Guimaraes’ knowledge of the opposition, he will have to assist the visitors to maintain control of the midfield battle.

Saliba is now back in contention after recovering from a back injury. The Frenchman has not played in the first team this season, but has made two appearances as he recovers. He played 45 minutes for the U21s.

Arteta confirmed that Saliba is in good shape and will begin to play more games, though he is unlikely to be in the starting line-up for the game against Newcastle.

Konsa should be in the starting line-up alongside Gabriel. Saliba could come on from the bench, as he looks to make his first competitive appearance of the season after the Champions League final last time out.

Saka is still unavailable due to quad trouble, whilst Dowman is suspended. Madueke should start on the right and Havertz will spearhead the attack.

Newcastle United: Predicted line-up not confirmed in the supplied team news.

Arsenal: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Guimaraes; Madueke, Odegaard, Tzolis; Havertz.

Arsenal absentees: Martin Zubimendi, Bukayo Saka and Max Dowman.

Saliba is available but is not expected to start.

Newcastle have leaked goals at home this season. However, with Madueke and Tzolis providing pace in wide areas, this should not worry Arsenal too much.

Nevertheless, this game should be challenging for the Gunners. Newcastle are dangerous in attack and can capitalise on errors quickly in possession.

Despite Arsenal’s solid defensive record, they have failed to keep a clean sheet in their 4 visits to St James’ Park.

Overall this should be a good watch with goals scored by both sides. However, Arsenal should be able to pick up some vital 3 points.

Predicted score: Newcastle United 2-3 Arsenal.

Akram Jadid’s name has been in the headlines again recently, and for good reason given his exploits on international duty.

Calciomercato.com begin a report by stating that Ruben Amorim had already made a note of Jadid’s qualities, given that he called him up to first team training at the end of August, just days before the win against Venezia.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The coach has been ‘bewitched’ by the young talent, and it was a first opportunity for the teenager to work with the senior side. The staff also got to see exactly what level he is at, given that his scoring record gave him a reputation after netting over 700 goals in the lower levels.

Jadid represents another diamond in the youth sector for Milan, one that needs to be nurtured in the best possible way. Having risen up the age groups, he is currently a key player in Vito Michele Antonelli’s U18 team.

Last season, he was a key figure in the U15’s Scudetto victory, thanks in part to his goal in the final against Empoli. The fact he has been promoted multiple levels since says a lot about how he is through of internally.

The report described Jadid as ‘a lively, mobile left winger who enjoys constantly taking on opponents to create numerical superiority and finish, or pass (depending on the situation). He is a No.10 for his technical ability and vision, and a No.9 in the penalty area for his eye for goal’.

In this first part of the season, Jadid has made eight appearances – all as a starter – and has scored four goals against Atalanta, Inter and Lecce. He continued this good form for his country with a hat-trick for Morocco U17s in the Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers victory over Tunisia.

🇲🇦 #ACMilan youth star Akram Jadid scored a hat-trick inside five minutes for Morocco U17s ⭐️⚽⚽⚽

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 17, 2026

He scored three times in five minutes. The third goal was particularly impressive: after anticipating the opposing defender and pounced on a loose ball, Jadid moved inside, evaded the return of another opponent, and concluded his solo effort with a curling right-footed shot that left the goalkeeper with no chance.

What comes next? For now, Akram Jadid will continue to grow with the U18 side, but the plan is that in the coming weeks he will be tested in the Primavera, so as to be able to compete against an even higher level of opponents.

Amorim is keeping an eye on him. Given his propensity for working with young players and instilling their trust, it cannot be ruled out that Jadid could appear on the list of players called up for a Serie A match in the near future.

For now, the parallel with Francesco Camarda – another record-holder from the Rossoneri youth team – is intriguing. Milan are enjoying him, and the Italian Federation are also monitoring things, as they could try to ‘steal’ him from Morocco.

#2028. West Ham’s Home Advantage Problem Won’t Disappear With 60,000 Fans

Mark Noble has called on West Ham United supporters to help transform the London Stadium into an intimidating venue as Scott Parker prepares for his first home match in charge against Preston North End.

Speaking in an interview with the club’s official website, Noble praised the ‘extraordinary’ loyalty of West Ham fans following relegation and insisted that the club’s ambition remains an immediate return to the Premier League.

He also challenged supporters to make life uncomfortable for visiting teams, arguing that a crowd of 60,000 should give West Ham a significant advantage. But I think it’s important to point out that getting the fans onside and creating an intimidating atmosphere are probably two very different things.

There’s no doubt about it. When the London Stadium is loud, it is impressive, as anybody who attended that incredible night against Sevilla will testify.

But I do think it’s a long way from being intimidating.

For that to happen, I firmly believe supporters need to be close to the pitch.

Not just to cause opposition players discomfort, but to put pressure on referees and give West Ham the kind of home advantage that seems prevalent throughout the league.

The distance between the stands and the playing surface remains a fundamental problem, regardless of how many supporters are in attendance.

It’s something I’ve previously argued when discussing proposals to improve the stadium atmosphere.

Isolated tiers in the stadium and poor pitch proximity do little to help the atmosphere at the London Stadium

It was always my concern that relegation to the Championship would see visiting teams regard a trip to the London Stadium as a lovely day out in opulent surroundings. Opposition changing rooms are grand and palatial and their team coach can pull into the venue untroubled by home fans.

And our results in Stratford have certainly done little to disprove that theory. However, that doesn’t mean things can’t improve.

I genuinely believe that getting West Ham playing on the front foot will help eliminate some of the eerie silences we’ve heard so frequently at the London Stadium.

Noble wants supporters to see a team giving everything, and I think he’s absolutely right about that.

If Parker can produce an aggressive, attacking side that gives the crowd something to get excited about, the atmosphere should improve considerably.

But turning the London Stadium into a genuinely intimidating venue is another matter entirely.

And unfortunately, that’s a problem which can’t be solved simply by asking 60,000 people to make more noise.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

With over a decade of professional sports media experience, he is a frequent West Ham United analyst and contributor for Sky Sports News, BBC Football Focus, and BBC Radio 5 Live. He previously served as an official video and content creator for West Ham United FC during the club's tenure at Upton Park and featured in the official documentary commemorating the historic final game at the Boleyn Ground.

A lifelong Hammer since the legendary 10-0 victory over Bury, when he isn't providing daily match analysis on the Hammers Chat YouTube Channel or broadcasting on X (@GONZObignose), he can be found walking his dog and restoring classic pinball machines.

Looking at all of the top games on TV, the stadia are considerably worse than London Stadium for proximity of fans.

Maybe we just lack the pyrotechnics in the crowd. The mad grabbing and jostling of inferior beings next to us. The joy of trying to intimidate anyone. We also lack a car park to show off our loutish best.

Whatever you think of the stadium, great and intimidating atmospheres can be choreographed to deliver at kick off, but if the team start sluggishly and without energy then that atmosphere will quickly deflate.

We were famously close to the pitch at Upton Park and won nothing for decades.

Blaming the stadium is just a distraction from the fact that we’re not playing well; when Andy Carroll scored that overhead kick against Palace, no one near me said they didn’t appreciate because they weren’t closer to the pitch.

If the ‘quality’ of the stadium is so important, explain Spurs to me…

#2026. The curious case of Sebastien Pocognoli looks certain to have a grisly ending... the SFA have hired a dud

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 14:13 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 14:26 EST, 17 November 2026

Of all the many stories written by F Scott Fitzgerald, one of the finest authors and wordsmiths of his time, The Great Gatsby will forever remain his masterpiece.

In some of his other work written as he travelled across Europe, Fitzgerald also had a line about Switzerland, describing it as a ‘country where very few things begin, but many things end.’

It is a curious quote and, like much of Fitzgerald’s work, is open to interpretation. As the man who also wrote The Curious Case of Benjamin Button, curiosity was a common theme.

As for the Curious Case of Sebastien Pocognoli, Switzerland may, indeed, be the country where everything came to an end.

What unfolded in St Gallen on Monday evening was a horror show. Scotland were battered 4-0 by Switzerland’s B team. There is no way to sugar-coat a result like that, no way to dress it up as anything other than an embarrassment. They played OK for half an hour and then fell apart.

Pocognoli claimed afterwards that there were positives to be taken and how some of Scotland’s football was the best they have produced across his six matches in charge.

Sebastien Pocognoli is facing serious questions after a miserable Nations League campaign

Utter nonsense. That was a manager clutching at straws at the end of a Nations League campaign which has been an unmitigated disaster pretty much from start to finish.

Let’s go back to the very start here. After Steve Clarke had pushed the Scottish Football Association (SFA) into awarding him a new four-year contract, only to then walk away after the World Cup, it was a chance for a fresh start.

On the day when Pocognoli was unveiled as the new head coach in August, Ian Maxwell and Craig Mulholland, the SFA’s chief executive and chief football officer, were beaming with positivity.

They told us all how data and AI had been used in the recruitment process, and how several clubs across Europe had been chasing Pocognoli.

They clearly viewed it as a coup to have landed the 39-year-old Belgian, who had won a league title in his homeland with Union Saint-Gilloise before a short stint with Monaco.

What would the data say now? Six games played, two wins, a draw and three defeats, five goals scored and ten conceded, seven points and a lousy third-placed finish in Group B1.

Both of those wins came against a North Macedonian side who lost all six of their games. They were a pub team – and Scotland still struggled to beat them at Hampden last Friday night.

Pocognoli was unable to inspire any resistance as his side succumbed to defeat in St Gallen

Scotland lost 7-0 on aggregate to Switzerland over the two games. Against Slovenia, a 0-0 draw on the opening day in Ljubljana was then followed with a woeful 2-1 defeat at Hampden.

All of which begs a very simple question. Where, exactly, are the grounds for optimism here? How is this getting any better?

When Pocognoli arrived, he spoke about trying to change the style of play, get Scotland playing a more exciting brand of football, whilst bringing through a new generation of players.

It was not a rebuild. He inherited a group of players who were accustomed to success under Clarke and who qualified for three tournaments out of a possible four.

His remit was to help Scotland take the next step in major tournaments. With a more dynamic style of play, the job was to help the nation take the next step.

There has been no revolution thus far. No evidence whatsoever that this coach is capable of delivering results nor a better style of play.

There is no satisfaction to be taken in any of this. When Pocognoli was appointed, it was, in the eyes of this observer, an interesting and progressive move.

SFA chiefs Craig Mulholland and Ian Maxwell proudly unveil new boss Pocognoli at Hampden

Over the past 48 hours or so, there has been a lot of revisionism from some folk about Clarke. ‘Aye, the grass isn’t always greener...’

That’s garbage. Clarke’s time was up with Scotland. He should never have been handed a new four-year deal in the first place. At least he did the right thing in resigning after the World Cup.

The whole thing was finished. The problem is that the SFA look like they have appointed a total dud as his successor. Both of those things can be true at the same time.

It is also worth remembering that the only reason we arrived at Pocognoli is because Clarke walked away. The SFA did not instigate any change.

The hiring of a new head coach was not a proactive change of direction, but a reactive move from an executive body who became accepting of Clarke’s limitations and allowed him to position them over a barrel.

Listen, there is nothing inherently wrong with using data and metrics in football. It’s the modern way. Using data to inform decisions and recruitment processes is smart business.

But the data in itself is no guarantee of success. There are some intangibles in football, things which are harder to quantify. Like a manager who blindly sticks to a system which is patently ill-suited to the players at his disposal.

Things like leadership and communication skills. We can cut Pocognoli some slack in that English is not his first language. He comes across as a thoroughly decent and likeable chap. He’s doing his best. He wants to embrace the culture and makes an effort to sing the National Anthem.

Scotland's defeat arose from individual mistakes, a common theme during the Belgian's reign

All of that is undoubtedly to be welcomed. Good on him. But would anyone describe him as an inspirational figure?

When you listen to him speak, have you ever felt slightly confused in terms of the message he’s actually trying to get across?

How must that sound in the dressing room? When Andy Robertson spoke post-match on Monday night, there was frustration in his voice.

The captain insisted there is simply no time or patience with these things. Scotland need to deliver results now.

To be fair, there actually would be a degree of patience shown by the Tartan Army towards Pocognoli if there was something to actually believe in.

There was a lot of goodwill towards him at the start. If there were signs across these last six games that he could deliver a more exciting team to watch, they would show patience.

But on the basis of what we’ve seen so far, there’s been absolutely nothing to suggest he can move this team forward. Ask yourself a very simple question – do Scotland pass the eye test?

Are we seeing a team who are playing on the front foot and creating chances? The answer, obviously, is no.

Steve Clarke celebrates Scotland's win over Denmark a year ago... how fans miss such highs

Many Scotland fans are now confronting the possibility that we might not even qualify for Euro 2028, a tournament which we are co-hosting.

By finishing third in the Nations League, we will now be in pot three for the Euro qualifiers and will face a more difficult group.

Beyond that, we would be relying on the back-door method of one of the best-placed home nations not to qualify directly.

Those Euro qualifiers will start in March of next year. Does Pocognoli even make it that far? Or should the SFA hold their hands up, admit they’ve made a mistake, and rectify it?

That feels unlikely. But on the basis of what we have seen over these first six games, it’s hard to see how this gets any better.

We are worse now than we were at the end under Clarke. Much, much worse. This is not teething problems. It’s a team who have regressed massively under a head coach who was supposed to move the whole thing forward.

#2023. European hero still has a vital role to play as expectation rises ahead of Preston clash | West Ham News

West Ham’s veteran midfielder has been the subject of an honest interview in his home country on Czech radio coinciding with the release of his autobiography. One of the more revealing comments Tomas Soucek made concerns the pressure and the expectation of playing in front of a big audience – such as West Ham will undoubtedly face tomorrow as the season re-commences with a home tie at London Stadium in front of 60,000 expectant supporters.

Unlike several others, from his words it is clear that Soucek seems to thrive on the pressure and the weight of expectation upon him. As one of only a handful of medal winners still at the club from the 2023 campaign, Soucek’s experience should become a steadying influence in the dressing room even though he mostly starts games on the bench these days.

Handling the weight of expectation at London Stadium has been daunting at times

‘Tornado Tom’ reveals that, far from letting it get to him, he actually enjoys the weight of expectation and pressure :

“Yes, obviously I feel it, but I like the pressure. Because football is always up and down, you have so many wins and so many losses – and it’s up to you how you recover from all of it.

“And I love that. As you said, it’s the most watched league in the world. And West Ham’s fans are crazy – they’re the best in the league, and it’s such a historic club.

“From the first day until now, I think me and West Ham connection is as good as it could possibly be in all aspects.

“And, yes, the pressure is there, but I try to work with it – and that’s why we play football.” (englishradio.cz)

The pressure will be significantly eased with a clean sheet and three points tomorrow – whether Soucek now, 31 gets into the action or simply acts as a calming figure in the dressing room. He is one of those very rare characters in the West Ham team – a leader on and off the pitch – and in another era could have spent years as the club’s captain.

#2018. West Ham’s Forgotten Wonderkid Lands Surprise Lifeline

Back in June, I wrote about a former West Ham academy graduate, a player once tipped for stardom after bursting onto the scene as a teenager. Many believed he had all the attributes needed to become a Premier League regular and potentially an England international. Sadly, football does not always follow the script, and Reece Oxford’s career gradually drifted away from the spotlight.

His move to German side Augsburg initially appeared to be the perfect opportunity to develop away from the intense scrutiny of English football. However, injuries and setbacks limited his impact, and after seven years with the Bundesliga club he departed in 2025 having made just 80 appearances.

Fast forward to this week and Oxford has been handed a fresh opportunity after Bromley announced the signing of the 27-year-old defender. The move could prove to be exactly what both player and club need.

There were high hopes for Reece oxford’s career: At still only 27 he has a chance of better times ahead

Karl Robinson, recently appointed manager of the Greater London  outfit, faces a significant challenge with Bromley currently sitting at the foot of League One. The Ravens will hope Oxford can provide a much-needed boost as the club look to climb the table.

Oxford has already spoken positively about the move, saying: “I’ve been here for a few weeks now getting my fitness levels up. Everyone has been great. All I can do is give something back to them now.”

Away from the media pressure that once followed his every step, this could be the ideal environment for Oxford to rebuild his confidence and rediscover the talent that once made him one of English football’s brightest prospects.

Everyone at C&H wishes him every success in the next chapter of his career.

#2014. GdS: Two games, one shot and an angry team-mate – ‘nightmare’ for Ramos extends to Portugal

AC Milan welcomed back a rejuvenated Goncalo Ramos after the last international break, but they will not do so this time.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, Ramos is finding himself ‘trapped in a nightmare season’, which is now also taking its toll on him for the national team too. As a reminder, he scored three goals in three starts (against Norway, Denmark and Norway again) during the September-October break.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

This allowed him to put his struggles behind him for a couple of weeks, but things are now getting tough with the Seleção as well. Last Saturday – in a 4-1 defeat against Denmark – he finished the match without even touching the ball in the penalty box.

It was frighteningly similar to the isolation seen at Milan, and the problem is that his numbers didn’t improve even in Wales. Portugal won 3-2 but not only did the former PSG man not get his name on the scoresheet, he also didn’t participate in any of the goals directly.

His numbers in the 59 minutes he was on the pitch: 1 shot attempted (a header from Neto’s pass from the left in the 47th minute), 4/7 successful passes, 11 touches, and 1 unsuccessful dribble. The story of a striker who is not involved.

That’s not all, either. Gonçalo also angered Bruno Fernandes. It happened during a counter-attack, with the Portuguese captain breaking down the left and crossing low, expecting Ramos to be there. Gonçalo had stopped though, and Fernandes’s reprimand was inevitable.

The two would later have another exchange at the end of the match, with Bruno reminding his team-mate – who was disappointed to be brought off after less than an hour – of the responsibility of replacing a giant like Cristian Ronaldo. Oh, and Bruno Fernandes has been linked today, by the way.

In short, Goncalo Ramos is ‘twisted in a spiral he can’t seem to escape’. After the game in Cardiff last night, he has reached 661 minutes without a goal for club and country. The last one was exactly a month ago, on October 18th against Atalanta.

#2013. Man United Confidential: Mauricio Pochettino to be given money to spend in January as club target recruits in THREE positions - and surprise at popular coach's sacking

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER

Published: 12:00 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 15:04 EST, 17 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino’s whirlwind arrival as Manchester United’s new head coach has left little time to work out where he will live – but a key factor in that decision will be his beloved dog Sansa.

Pochettino will leave the TQL Stadium in Cincinnati after the USA’s game against Haiti in the early hours of Wednesday morning and go straight to the airport to catch an eight-hour flight to Manchester on board a private jet paid for by United.

The club will also provide him with somewhere to live as he settles into the new job and finds a more permanent residence.

The 54-year-old, who also has a home in Barcelona, is said to have lived just outside London when he was Tottenham manager and then spent the entirety of his 18-month spell as Paris Saint-Germain boss in a luxury hotel.

Pochettino lived in Knightsbridge while he was in charge of Chelsea, and revealed that he enjoyed getting feedback from fans while out on his daily 90-minute dog walks with Sansa.

He named the Rhodesian Ridgeback after a character from Game of Thrones and has even given the dog her own Instagram account.

Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of the US national team for the final time in the early hours of Wednesday morning, then head straight to Manchester on a private jet

Pochettino (pictured with his son Maurizio) will have to find accommodation which suits his dog Sansa, a Rhodesian Ridgeback (Source: Instagram/pochettino)

Describing the difficulty of Spurs playing on a Saturday night in 2018, he said: ‘At 7pm, I am normally on my sofa with my dog Sansa watching the Spanish league because they start at 7.45pm, or France because Ligue 1 starts at 8pm, or Italy, or different games.

‘It will be so strange for my dog. Not for me but my dog. “Where is my dad?” she is going to say. She is beautiful and I am in love with her.’

The living habits of United bosses have varied over the years. Sir Alex Ferguson, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Ruben Amorim favoured Wilmslow and Alderley Edge, David Moyes remained further afield in Lytham, Louis van Gaal and Erik ten Hag chose Hale, and Jose Mourinho famously spent 895 days at the Lowry Hotel in Manchester (where dogs can stay for an additional £30).

United have no plans to change the timings for Wednesday’s training session, even though Pochettino and four of his backroom team may not arrive at Carrington until the early afternoon.

The private jet carrying the Argentine, first-team coach Miguel D’Agostino, strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott should touch down from Cincinnati around noon.

An advance party of three more coaches – Pochettino’s assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez, and his son and fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino – have been in Manchester since Sunday after they were released early by the US Soccer Federation as a gesture of goodwill following the 6-0 first-leg win over Haiti in the quarter-finals of the North American equivalent of the Nations League.

They took training on Tuesday as United’s players continue to report back from international duty, and will also oversee the session on Wednesday morning after United decided not to reschedule it so Pochettino could be present.

The Argentine will be firmly hands-on from Thursday, though, as he prepares for his first game against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

Pochettino, who will speak to club media shortly after his arrival before conducting his first press conference on Friday, has faced Liverpool 19 times in his managerial career, losing 11 games, drawing five and winning three.

Pochettino's assistant Jesus Perez (right) has been in Manchester since Sunday and took training on Tuesday

Strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya - the first woman to be part of United's backroom staff - will travel with Pochettino to Manchester following the Haiti game

Pochettino will inherit a team in the relegation zone – which could even be bottom of the Premier League by kick-off on Sunday – and it’s understood he will be given modest funds to improve his squad in the January transfer window.

United are in desperate need of a left back and a striker, having failed to sign cover in both positions in the summer.

One potential target may be US centre forward Folarin Balogun who has prospered under Pochettino but only started once for Monaco this season after a summer move to Everton fell through. United sources say the new head coach will have input in the weeks ahead before a clearer plan emerges.

United also want a centre back after Confidential revealed last week that Fulham’s Calvin Bassey and Nathan Collins, of Brentford, are two options being considered.

It’s possible that one of those deals may have to be a loan, however, with United’s delicate financial situation set to be spelt out in black and white when the results from the first quarter of the financial year are released on Thursday.

Although Pochettino is going to have money for new players, United will have to be smart in their transfer dealings and spend wisely.

In the short term, Luke Shaw and Marcus Rashford may be available again for the first time in more than a month against Liverpool.

However, there is a concern over Patrick Dorgu who was deemed to be unfit for international duty with Denmark, even though he returned to action for Michael Carrick’s final game after a month-and-a-half out with a hamstring injury and headed a stoppage-time equaliser in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa.

Fulham's Calvin Bassey (right) is among the centre-back options United are considering

Marcus Rashford may be available for the first time in more than a month against Liverpool

It was the departure of Travis Binnion, rather than Carrick, that raised the most eyebrows among figures working in football over the past few days.

Agents and first-team players privately described their surprise at seeing Binnion – a long-time academy figure before stepping up to the first team to help Darren Fletcher as interim and then Carrick – leave the club.

United have cleaned house for the arrival of Pochettino’s backroom team, and Binnion was one of those who paid the price.

A popular figure in the dressing room, Joshua Zirkzee, Benjamin Sesko and Kobbie Mainoo are among the players who are known to have enjoyed working with Binnion.

Despite stepping up to the first team, where he would watch matches from the press box alongside United’s team of analysts, Binnion remained in contact with numerous academy player representatives to ensure their development was progressing as planned.

Binnion, who first arrived in 2019 as an Under 16s coach and progressed to the Under 18s, Under 21s and then head of player development and coaching, isn’t expected to be out of the game for too long though.

Agency sources believe rival Premier League academies will move quickly to recruit him, with Everton seen as one potential landing spot. United’s former academy head Nick Cox is now Everton technical director and has already recruited Dave Hughes and Tom Curtis, who worked under Binnion at United.

A popular figure in the dressing room, Joshua Zirkzee, Benjamin Sesko and Kobbie Mainoo are among the players who enjoyed working with Travis Binnion (pictured)

Your responses to our 36-man Manchester United squad audit have made for interesting reading over the last week.

Confidential pored over the first-team squad, as well as numerous rising stars in the academy, that Pochettino and his staff will quickly have to run the rule over.

While some of the voting went as expected – your votes demonstrated an overwhelming desire among the fanbase to see Noussair Mazraoui, Diogo Dalot, Shaw and Harry Maguire leave this summer – there were a few surprises.

Many voted for captain Bruno Fernandes, who just recently rejected a second contract extension offer, to be moved on, along with Rashford. Amad Diallo and summer signing Andrey Santos are two who divide opinion, but both made the cut.

Check out the full squad audit HERE to see how others voted and leave your own verdict!

Confidential understands JJ Gabriel’s representatives held fresh talks with Real Madrid at the club’s training ground on Monday as a move to the Santiago Bernabeu edges ever closer.

Now that Gabriel has officially announced a partnership with Epic Sports Agency, his agent Ali Barat is leading negotiations and has been at Real’s Valdebebas headquarters along with the 16-year-old and his family.

Gabriel announced his departure from the club in an Instagram video on Tuesday night, as he and the Spanish giants hope to get a move over the line.

JJ Gabriel's representatives have held fresh talks with Real Madrid as his move to the Bernabeu edges closer

Eric Cantona and Sir Alex Ferguson will reunite next month at a special screening of the Frenchman’s new documentary.

Cantona: Flower of Evil won rave reviews in France and is now heading to the UK, with a one-night-only panel featuring Cantona and Ferguson at Aviva Studios in Manchester on December 7.

The documentary film digs deeper into how Ferguson channelled Cantona’s brilliance and honed his explosiveness – a trait that had seen him branded ‘unmanageable’ in France. Tickets range from £156 all the way up to £1,000. You can purchase them here.

#2012. West Ham 1 – 1 Preston North End | Player ratings as Parker drops more points

West Ham again conceded in the first half and spent the rest of the game peppering Preston’s goal – four efforts hit the woodwork but to no avail until Mavropanos’ second half equaliser. A lack of clinical finishing cost Scott Parker’s side dear as the points were shared.

Encouraging early touches with his feet and a willingness to catch rather than punch initially inspired confidence. Failed to get his fists to a corner, the ball striking Piroe on the head and looping over Herrick to give Preston a simple goal to create their lead. A superb double save just before half-time kept West Ham in touch after Mayers’ poor header. Grew in stature in the second half, notably catching balls where Hermansen might have punched.

Good early interplay with Bowen down the right. Unlucky not to score when his effort crashed against the post immediately after Bowen had hit the woodwork. Replaced by Souček on 78 minutes.

Solid enough first half without really being tested. Slipped in to meet a deflected Engels cross and equalise in true Mavropanos style.

Looked far more comfortable in the combative centre-back role, without being seriously tested for pace. Met Solomon’s second half cross with a header that was blocked.

Solid enough first half until a dreadful defensive header gifted the ball back to Preston, with Herrick rescuing him through a superb double save. Booked after misjudging his control and pulling down an opponent. Replaced by Scarles on 78 minutes.

A great through ball released Piroe for West Ham’s first decent opportunity. Excellent work out wide, crossing with his weaker foot to allow Mavropanos to equalise. Lots of wide running in a much more advanced position than under Nuno. Looked better for it.

Making his first appearance of the season, showed little sign of rustiness. Should have equalised after a well-worked corner, curling into the side-netting. Looked increasingly at home sitting in front of the defence and moving remarkably quickly across the turf. Quick feet in the opposition box led to a shot poked agonisingly close, but just wide. A pretty good shift on his return; surprising he lasted until 90 minutes, when Magassa replaced him.

Should have taken a first-time shot with his right foot, but instead shifted onto his favoured left and scuffed the chance in the first half. Needs to produce more. Evidently Parker agrees as he was replaced by Castellanos on 57 minutes.

Struck the post with a right-footed effort as West Ham pressed for an equaliser. Had the beating of his full-back in the second half, making frequent runs down the right and crossing with his weaker foot. Several shots but lacked that killer punch – as did the whole attack.

Should have opened the scoring after ten minutes when sent through one-on-one by Engels, but the goalkeeper saved. Lots of trying and ‘nearlies’ but too little output. Booked on 82 minutes for a professional foul. Not enough from the striker.

A decent early effort from 25 yards went straight at the goalkeeper. Immediately after the restart, stepped inside and struck the bar with a brilliant curling right-footed shot. Replaced by Solomon on 57 minutes at which point West Ham’s pace and zip largely vanished. There’s a lesson in there…

On for Austbø, 57 minutes. One jinking run inside produced a cross met by Morato’s head, but the effort was blocked. Looked very right-footed and unable to beat defenders on the outside. West Ham were poorer for the substitution of Austbø and Solomon’s introduction.

On for Mukasa, 57 minutes. Fluffed his lines on 85 minutes, looping a back-post header over the bar.

On for Mayers, 78 minutes. One decent cross late on. Understandably rusty-looking.

On for Veltman, 78 minutes. Almost won it in the 94th minute with a back-post header tipped over by Preston’s goalkeeper.
